plan.notes: Source: official UK Pigman College of Engineering pathway sheet, 'Computer Science 2025-2026 (Pathway from Bellarmine University)', https://ptc.engr.uky.edu/sites/default/files/2025-11/bellarmine-university-major-sheets-25-26.pdf . Catalog year 2025-2026 is printed in the sheet title. Transcription method: direct PDF text extraction (pdftotext -layout) from the downloaded official PDF, cross-checked against the parallel 'Computer Science 2025-2026 (Pathway from Union Commonwealth University)' sheet (https://engr.uky.edu/sites/default/files/2025-11/union-commonwealth-university-major-sheets-25-26.pdf); the UK Course Pathway columns are byte-identical between the two - only the partner-school transfer-equivalency column differs. TRANSFER-PATHWAY FRAMING VERDICT: standard UK sequence. Although each document is titled 'Pathway from <partner school>', the 'UK Course Pathway' column is the standard native-UK four-year term-by-term sequence: it begins Freshman Year First Semester with standard UK freshman courses (EGR 101/102, CHE 105, CIS/WRD 110, MA 113) and spans all 8 semesters. Transfer students are framed as a VARIANT of this sequence, not its subject: sheet footnote § states 'Transfer students will take EGR 215, Introduction to the Practice of Engineering for Transfer Students, in place of EGR 101 and EGR 103', and footnote † notes transfer students may satisfy UK Core Arts and Creativity via EGR 215. The 'Transfer Courses' column (partner-school equivalents, e.g. Bellarmine CS 130 for EGR 102) was intentionally omitted as partner-specific articulation. Equivalencies in TES as of 10/2025 (per sheet). Caveats: (1) The sheet publishes no per-course prerequisites, so all prereq arrays are empty and external_prereqs is empty; the only progression rule is Engineering Standing: courses marked with * (MA 114, CS 215, CS 217, CS 218, CS 275) require successful completion with at least a 2.5 GPA in those courses plus cumulative UK GPA of at least 2.5; if a course is repeated, the best grade is used. (2) CS 499 Senior Design Project is the Graduation Composition and Communication Requirement (GCCR) course (sheet marker ∞). (3) EE 280 course title transcribed verbatim from the sheet as 'Design of Logic Design' (as printed; confirmed identical in both sheet versions). (4) EGR 101 and EGR 103 together fulfill the UK Core Arts and Creativity requirement (sheet footnote †). (5) CIS/WRD 110/111 each require also completing one of COM 181, COM 252, COM 281, or COM 287 for students taking ENG 101/102 (sheet footnote Δ). (6) PHY 241 lab taken only if enrolled in PHY 231 (sheet footnote ‡). (7) Free Elective [E]: 3 of the 7 credits are not to be selected from computer science, mathematics, natural science and engineering. Credit total 129 = term sums 14+18+17+16+15+18+16+15.
